rule: Each cell of a coloured sequence line emits diagonal rays forming nested chevrons (sequence repeated shifted along diagonals), and the edge marker bars flood their colour into the triangular regions bounded by those diagonals, leaving the rest background.
gap: Needs diagonal rays from every sequence cell with overwrite order, then chained region fill by border marker colour inside the ray-bounded wedges.

rule: Each small arrow-shaped object with one odd-coloured tip cell shoots a dotted (every second cell) ray of the tip colour in the direction it points, and the grid edge it hits is painted entirely in that colour (corner where two painted edges meet becomes 0).
gap: Ray direction must be inferred from the arrow shape's orientation; needs period-2 dotted rays and painting the whole hit border line.

rule: Small objects slide vertically as rigid bodies toward the border row of their own colour (top or bottom) until they touch that border or previously stacked objects.
gap: Gravity direction must be chosen per object by matching its colour to the same-coloured border row.

rule: The grid contains several crossing straight lines (horizontal, vertical, diagonal); output a 1-row list of their colours ordered by stacking depth, from the line drawn underneath to the line on top at crossings.
gap: Needs occlusion relation between lines at crossing cells, a topological sort into depth order, and emitting colours as a sequence.

rule: The centre cell has a colour matching one of the noisy quadrant patterns; erase everything and draw a diagonal ray from the centre cell toward the corner of the quadrant containing that colour.
gap: Ray direction must be selected by matching centre colour to the quadrant with same-colour pattern; then clear all other content.

rule: Vertical bars on the floor exchange attributes: bar colours rotate one step right (cyclically) while bar heights rotate one step left.
gap: Needs object attribute decomposition (colour vs height) with separate cyclic permutations across the ordered set of bars.

rule: A bent 5-coloured key path runs from a coloured end to a 4 end: the background becomes the end colour, the 3x3 ring is translated by the key's end-to-end displacement vector, and diagonal 4-lines radiate from the ring's corners to the grid edges.
gap: Must read a glyph as a displacement vector plus background colour, translate the ring accordingly, then chain diagonal corner rays.

rule: Each row has one dominant colour C plus noise; output row is C exactly where the input row is not C, and 0 elsewhere (complement of that colour's mask).
gap: Needs a per-row (panel-by-row) dominant colour and mask-complement operation; no module keys rows as units with a complement.

rule: Each 9-object contains a zigzag crack of 6 cells; the 6 cells are removed and the object splits along the crack into two halves that each move one cell away from the crack (perpendicular to it).
gap: Needs splitting an object into parts along an internal marker line and moving each part apart, a part-level action.

rule: Each colour-1 object is recoloured and pushed to a side edge (keeping its row): objects that are solid or have a fully enclosed hole become 2 and move to the left edge; objects whose hole is open to the outside become 3 and move to the right edge.
gap: Needs open-vs-closed hole topology as a cue selecting both recolour and move direction to the grid edge per object.

rule: Find the object whose holes (background-coloured gaps) exactly match the shapes of loose small pieces elsewhere; output that object cropped with its holes filled by the matching pieces' colours.
gap: Needs shape-matching of loose pieces to holes, selecting the object they fit, and compositing pieces into holes.

rule: In each multicolour 3x3 patch the four corner cells rotate 90 degrees counter-clockwise while the four edge-middle cells rotate 90 degrees clockwise; centre unchanged.
gap: Needs part-wise transforms within an object (corners vs edges get opposite rotations), colour-agnostic; object-level D8 cannot split parts.

rule: Within each row, when a specific colour pair occurs ({1,8} or {4,7}), the right-hand cell slides left until it touches the left-hand cell; other pairs stay put.
gap: Move-until-contact must be gated by a learned colour-pair compatibility ({1,8},{4,7}) between single cells in the same row.

rule: Every solid square loses its outer ring (shrinks by one cell on each side, 3x3 becomes its centre), while the single isolated cell grows into a 9x9 square centred on itself.
gap: Needs colour-agnostic, size-keyed object change (erode ring / grow 1x1 to 9x9); test single cell has unseen colour 0.

rule: The top-left motif (bordered by an L of a border colour) is expanded fractally: each foreground cell becomes a copy of the motif and each background cell becomes the motif recoloured with the border colour; this block pattern is then tiled to fill the grid.
gap: Needs chained crop-motif, fractal self-substitution with border-colour recolour for background cells, then periodic tiling to the input size.

rule: A corner legend of colour pairs (a b) says shape colour a gets a halo colour b: each shape's bounding box padded by one cell becomes a 7x7 square where exterior background is painted b (enclosed holes stay 0).
gap: Legend lookup exists, but the action must be painting the padded-bbox exterior background around each shape, not recolouring or hole filling.

rule: In a 1/0 checkerboard with one 8 on an edge, all 1s in each line slide toward the 8's edge (compacting); in the 8's own line the 1s pack against the 8 and an equal number of 9s is written right after them.
gap: Needs cell-level compaction toward the marker's edge (direction from marker position) plus writing a run of 9s whose length equals the 1-count.

rule: A cross of divider lines splits the grid off-centre; the pattern in one quadrant is mirrored across the divider lines into the other quadrants (4-fold reflection about the cross, clipped at the grid edge).
gap: Mirror symmetry must use the off-centre separator lines as axes and allow clipping; self-model assumes grid-centred global symmetry.

rule: Each interior object is an arrow; the frame cell where the arrow points (in line with its shaft) takes the arrow's colour and the frame cell at the opposite end of that line becomes 0.
gap: Needs reading each object's pointing direction from its shape and marking frame cells at both ends of its axis.

rule: Objects of size 4 or more fall straight down (rigidly) until they hit the bottom edge; objects of size 3 or less stay in place.
gap: Gravity must apply only to objects passing a size threshold (>=4 cells); small objects are exempt.

rule: The 8 rectangle projects bands of 4 (its full width vertically and full height horizontally) to all grid edges; the bands paint over background and colour-2 objects but pass beneath colour-1 objects.
gap: Rays must be object-wide bands in four directions with colour-specific layering (overwrite 2, keep 1).

rule: A diagonal 1-segment is extended as a ray; it passes straight through colour-3 lines (overwriting the crossing cell with 1) but reflects off colour-2 lines like a mirror, continuing to the grid edge.
gap: Needs diagonal ray extension with reflection (bounce) at obstacles and colour-dependent pass-through vs reflect behaviour.

rule: Draw an orthogonal path of 8 from one marker cell to the other, travelling alongside walls and crossing each wall line only through its gate (the middle of its coloured segment), overwriting the gate cell.
gap: Needs path routing between two markers that threads through gate segments in successive wall lines.

rule: In the 5x1 column swap the first two cells and swap the last two cells, keeping the middle cell; i.e. a fixed positional permutation regardless of colours.
gap: Needs a learned fixed cell-position permutation (swap rows 0/1 and 3/4) with colours copied from input; not a D8 transform.

rule: Several framed rectangles each carry small marker sub-patterns; output the largest frame with the smaller pieces nested inside it, each placed so that its marker pattern coincides with the matching marker in the frame that contains it (docking by shared marks).
gap: Needs hierarchical assembly: nest objects inside one another by aligning matching sub-patterns, then crop to the outer frame.

rule: Count the two scattered speck colours; output (fixed 16x16, background 7) a bottom-left rectangle of 2 whose height is the minority count and width the majority count, with a 4 V-shape of diagonals rising from its bottom corners.
gap: Needs numerosity of colours mapped to rectangle dimensions, plus drawing a diagonal V pattern inside it.

rule: Specks of 8 lying inside the 2 region are erased, while 8 specks lying in the 7 region grow by one cell toward the 9 border line (wherever that border is).
gap: Speck action depends on enclosing region colour and growth direction comes from the distant 9 border; local tables lack this non-local cue.

rule: Count the cells of each colour (non-background); render each colour as a solid k x k square with k*k = its count, arranged left to right in ascending size, bottom-aligned, separated by one background column.
gap: Needs per-colour cell counts mapped to square sizes, sorting by count, and assembling a new output layout.

rule: Scattered single noise cells are removed except that the repeated noise colour is drawn as a right triangle in the corner toward which the diagonal line shape points; triangle leg length appears to equal the number of noise cells minus one (unsure of exact size and colour-selection rule).
gap: Needs noise-cell counting to size a corner triangle, choosing the corner from the line's pointing direction, and colour selection among noise.

rule: Legend rows/columns outside a 2-coloured diamond give one colour per row/column; inside the diamond each such row/column is filled by a ray of its legend colour growing from the diamond edge on the legend's side until it hits an interior obstacle or the far edge.
gap: Needs a position-aligned colour legend mapped to rows/columns, plus rays confined to the diamond interior that stop at obstacles.

rule: Colour-mask fractal: each input cell of colour c is replaced by an n x n block equal to the input's mask of colour c painted in c (other cells 0).
gap: Fractal variant where each block is the mask of cells equal to that cell's colour, not the plain non-zero mask.

rule: Copy the objects of the small left panel into the empty wider right panel, keeping rows but re-laying out horizontally by anchoring: full-width bars stretch to the new width, left-aligned objects stay left, right-aligned objects move to the right side.
gap: Needs anchor-aware non-uniform rescaling (stretch spans, preserve left/right alignment) from one panel to a differently sized panel.

rule: Each 3x3 ring whose centre has colour c is repeated periodically (period 3) in the direction of the large object of colour c until it overlaps that object by two cells.
gap: Needs directed periodic extension of an object toward a same-colour target with a stopping condition (overlap into target).

rule: In a two-row alternating motif, every second motif row (the B rows) is cyclically shifted one cell to the right; the other rows are unchanged.
gap: Needs a colour-agnostic row-wise cyclic shift applied to alternate rows; learned local patterns are tied to seen colours.

rule: The motif at the bottom of the grid is tiled vertically upward with period equal to its height (aligned at the bottom), overwriting the empty background above.
gap: Periodic extension must treat the uniform background region as unknown and use bottom-anchored vertical period equal to the motif height.

rule: Keep only the two most frequent colours in the grid; every other colour becomes 7.
gap: Needs global colour-frequency ranking (top-2 colours) to decide which cells are recoloured to 7.

rule: A small block next to a larger block is pushed through it toward the grid edge (away from the third, anchor object); the pierced block splits in two with each half moving one cell outward to make room.
gap: Needs an object-interaction behaviour: projectile passing through another object that splits and parts sideways; direction inferred from layout.

rule: Horizontal lines divide the grid into bands each holding a striped pattern of the line colour; output 3x5: per band a bar of its colour whose length equals the number of solid rows in its pattern, a 9 column, and a 5 marking one band (selection rule for the 5 unclear).
gap: Needs counting repeated pattern rows per band, emitting counts as bar lengths in a summary grid, and placing the 5 indicator.

rule: In a 3x3 panel grid, two panels holding the 2-motif define an orientation; empty panels are filled with 5- and 8-coloured copies of the motif to complete a fixed Y-shaped configuration rotated in 45-degree steps around the centre panel (one demo with an already complete configuration maps to a blank 16x16 grid).
gap: Needs a panel-level configuration template matched under 45-degree rotations of the 8-neighbour ring, then recoloured motif copies placed.

rule: Count the 8-connected objects of each colour and draw a bottom-aligned bar chart (5 columns, height = max count): each colour gets a fixed column (5,2,8,9,6 order) with bar height equal to its object count.
gap: Needs per-colour object counting rendered as a histogram with a learned colour-to-column assignment and count-dependent output height.

rule: From the given 7/3 row, build rows downward every second row: a cell gets a colour where the row two above has a 3 flanked by two coloured cells, alternating 6 and 7 per generation, until no cells qualify (shrinking pyramid).
gap: Needs an iterated cellular-automaton step (local rule applied generation by generation with alternating output colour) until extinction.

rule: Each object resting on the 8 floor moves straight up by a number of rows equal to its own cell count.
gap: Translation distance must equal the object's size; dynamics only moves fixed offsets or until contact.

rule: The input is a lattice of separator rows/columns with content blocks; delete the separator/frame rows and columns and concatenate the remaining content cells (blocks at lattice positions) into a compact grid that shows the drawn path.
gap: Needs detecting irregular lattice/separator rows and columns and gluing the surviving sub-blocks into a new grid.

rule: The objects touching the four grid corners are cycled clockwise: each corner object is translated (unrotated) so that it sits in the next corner clockwise; all other objects stay.
gap: Needs selecting corner-anchored objects and a group-level cyclic permutation of corner positions with corner-anchored placement.

rule: In a noisy grid, solid monochrome regions are crossed by short paths of foreign (noise) cells; each such path is recoloured to the colour of its head cell (e.g. the cell at the region's edge), making a clean line through the region.
gap: Needs segmenting solid regions within dense random noise and identifying the foreign path inside, then recolouring it with its endpoint colour.

rule: Two 9 markers sit outside an 8 wall structure; recolour to 9 the route along the 8 wall lines connecting the two markers, taking the side of the structure away from the 7 cells (7s mark compartments the route must avoid).
gap: Needs path search along wall segments between two markers with avoidance constraints set by 7 cells.

rule: Diamond outlines are rescaled about their centres by colour: colour-2 diamonds shrink by one step (radius minus 1), colour-5 diamonds grow by one (a single 5 becomes a radius-1 ring), other colours unchanged; partially off-grid diamonds included.
gap: Needs concentric scaling of diamond rings (incl. off-grid centres), with direction chosen by object colour.

rule: A dotted 4 outline on the dot lattice becomes a solid frame; the dotted coloured pieces outside are solidified (filled across the lattice gaps) and packed inside the frame side by side in their original left-right/top-bottom order with one-cell gaps, and removed from outside.
gap: Needs lattice-aware solidification of dotted pieces and ordered packing of several pieces into a frame interior.

rule: Several arrow-like objects point their 1-cell tips at a common centre; the dominant one (apparently the largest) keeps its tip and grows one full row/column at its back, while every other object loses its tip cell.
gap: Needs relational comparison among converging objects (winner by size) and two different object actions: tip removal vs back extension.

rule: For each horizontal bar, write a single cell in the 5-marker's column on the bar's row whose colour encodes the bar's length (2->1, 3->4, 4->9, 5->6).
gap: Needs object length measured and mapped through a learned length-to-colour code, written at the marker column.

rule: Between the 1 region (top) and 6 region (bottom) with a jagged boundary, draw a 9 line from the top down the column where the 1 region reaches deepest, and a 4 line from the top down the column of the 6 region's highest peak, stopping at the 6.
gap: Needs boundary extremum detection (deepest/highest column of a region) to select where vertical rays of fixed colours are drawn.

rule: The grid is a lattice of identical 5x5 tiles except one corrupted tile; output the normal tile with 1 written at every cell where the corrupted tile differs from it.
gap: Panel module needs majority tile vs odd-one-out difference overlay, marking mismatching cells with a new colour 1.

rule: The grid consists of vertical colour bands of varying width (with sprinkled noise cells) that are reordered as rigid units; usually the first band moves to the end (cyclic left rotation), but one demo instead reverses, so the ordering cue (possibly the noise) is unclear.
gap: Needs segmenting colour bands (no separator lines) and permuting them as units with their internal noise; ordering rule unresolved.

rule: Two crossing marker-bearing lines are replaced by a compact woven block bounded by the marker positions: rows alternate between the cross-line colour and patterns interleaving marker colours with the other line's colour (exact construction unclear).
gap: Needs reading both lines' marker sequences and composing them into a 2D woven pattern within a marker-defined box.

rule: Cells of the same colour (two or more) are joined into one connected orthogonal path (straight or L-shaped segments) in that colour, routed around the 8 walls; singleton colours are left alone.
gap: Connect handles only aligned straight segments; needs L-shaped/tree routing between same-colour cells with obstacle avoidance.

rule: The 7 block travels along its row/column band to the 9 block's position (replacing it, its old spot cleared); every gate of 0-dot pairs it passes through on the way gets its gap filled with 2.
gap: Needs move-to-target (block onto same-size target) plus marking the traversed gates with a trace colour.
